abort.single_instance_allowed: Already configured. Only a single configuration possible.
abort.unsupported_version: hassette {server_version} serves API schema {api_schema_version}, but this integration needs schema {min_api_schema_version} or newer. Upgrade hassette, then add the integration again.

error.cannot_connect: Failed to connect to hassette. Check the URL, and that Home Assistant can reach it.
error.forbidden: hassette's API refused the request (403). A proxy or firewall rule in front of hassette is probably blocking Home Assistant.
error.invalid_url: Enter a URL without a username or password in it, such as http://192.168.1.10:8126.
error.redirected: hassette's API redirected to {location}. If that is a login page, add a bypass for /api/ to the proxy in front of hassette (see the README). If it is the https form of your URL, use that URL instead.
error.token_required: hassette needs a token from Home Assistant's address. Enter a web API token, or list Home Assistant's address in hassette's web_api.trusted_proxies.

data_description.api_token: hassette's web API token. Leave it blank only if hassette lists Home Assistant's address in web_api.trusted_proxies.

reauth_confirm.description: hassette at {url} rejected the stored token. Enter its current web API token.

data_description.api_token: hassette's web API token. Leaving it blank relies on hassette's web_api.trusted_proxies, which gives everything at Home Assistant's address full access to hassette's API.
data_description.url: The URL of your hassette server, including the port, such as http://192.168.1.10:8126.
data_description.verify_ssl: Turn this off only for a self-signed certificate.

reconfigure.description: Change how Home Assistant connects to hassette. Devices and their settings are kept.

data_description.api_token: hassette's web API token. Leaving it blank relies on hassette's web_api.trusted_proxies, which gives everything at Home Assistant's address full access to hassette's API.
data_description.url: The URL of your hassette server, including the port, such as http://192.168.1.10:8126.
data_description.verify_ssl: Turn this off only for a self-signed certificate.

user.description: Connect Home Assistant to your hassette server. Each hassette app becomes a device with a switch to start and stop it, a reload button, and a status sensor.

action_in_progress.message: Another action on this app is still running. Try again when it finishes.

action_timeout.message: hassette didn't confirm the action in time. It may still have run; the app's state updates on the next refresh.

blocked_by_filter.message: hassette's --app filter excludes this app, so it can't be started here.

forbidden.message: hassette's API refused the request (403). A proxy or firewall rule in front of hassette is probably blocking Home Assistant.

invalid_response.message: hassette sent a response this integration can't read. Check that the integration and hassette are both up to date.

not_bootstrapped.message: hassette hasn't finished starting up, so apps can't be started yet. Try again shortly.

not_found.message: hassette doesn't have this app in its config.

redirected.message: hassette's API redirected to {location}. If that is a login page, add a bypass for /api/ to the proxy in front of hassette.

telemetry_unavailable.message: hassette couldn't read its telemetry database, so it can't list apps.

unsupported_version.message: hassette {server_version} serves API schema {api_schema_version}, but this integration needs schema {min_api_schema_version} or newer. Upgrade hassette.

unsupported_version.description:
hassette {server_version} serves API schema {api_schema_version}, but the Hassette integration needs schema {min_api_schema_version} or newer, so its apps are unavailable in Home Assistant.

Upgrade hassette. The integration reconnects on its own within 10 minutes, and this message clears.
unsupported_version.title: hassette is too old for the Hassette integration
